content.text: There's a `POST /devices ← RenameDeviceRequest` endpoint. Let me see whether the app's `renameDevice` actually calls it, and the energy-role setter:

I dug into all three and they're the same root cause wearing three hats. Here's what I found, then where I'd push back.

## What's actually happening

**Balcony PV on the Eve** — it *is* sampled and logged (the Eve is in the controller's attribute cache and reports energy). The problem is classification: `classify()` tags every Matter device as `load`, and the `load` class only counts the **import** counter (`bk->load_wh += imp`). A back-feeding PV shows its generation on the **export** counter, which the load class discards. So it's logged, but its PV generation evaporates and never reaches `pv_wh`. You were right about the symptom, slightly off on the mechanism.

**Rename not syncing** — `renameDevice()` in the app is **local-only**; it never calls the controller (even though a `POST /devices` rename endpoint already exists). The chart legend name comes from the controller's CSV row, stamped at write time. So the app name and the graph name are two disconnected values — and historical rows bake the *old* name forever.

**The unifying cause:** the app and controller keep separate, unsynced device metadata. The app is where you rename and assign energy roles; neither ever reaches the controller. `assignEnergyRole()` is local-only too.

## Where I agree, and where I'd challenge you

You're right that **logging should key on a stable ID, not a name** — and it already does (node_id is in every row). Baking the name per-row is the redundant part.

But I'd **challenge "store the name on the controller"** as the fix for the graph. The app is already the source of truth for names — that's where you type them, and the series carries `node_id`. So the chart can just resolve `node_id → your app's device name` locally. That fixes renames **instantly**, retroactively (even for old data), with **zero firmware change and no round-trip**. Pushing names to the controller only earns its keep if a *non-app* consumer reads the log (a web UI, offline CSV analysis). If that's a goal, say so — otherwise it's motion without payoff.

**The name problem is app-side. The real controller-side gap is roles** — and that's what actually needs building, because the controller physically cannot classify your balcony PV (or a battery) without knowing the role. That's the same app→controller role-sync I flagged for battery; your balcony PV is now a second reason to build it. It'd classify the Eve as PV → generation lands in `pv_wh` and gets its own line.

So my counter-proposal, in two independent pieces:

questions.question: Name in the chart legend — where should it resolve from?

options.label: App resolves locally
options.description: Legend maps node_id → your app's device name. Fixes renames instantly + retroactively, no firmware change. Controller stops sending names (or keeps them only for offline CSV). Recommended.

options.label: Sync names to controller
options.description: App pushes renames via POST /devices; aggregation resolves the current name from the device record (not the stale CSV row). Needed only if a non-app consumer reads the log. More work, firmware flash.

questions.question: Energy-role sync (fixes balcony PV, unlocks battery) — build it now?

options.label: Build role sync now
options.description: App pushes each device's energy role to the controller; classify() uses role first (Eve→PV, battery→battery), profile heuristic as fallback. Fixes the balcony PV and unlocks battery-over-time. Needs proto + firmware + flash.

options.label: Design first, then build
options.description: I write up the role-sync design (endpoint shape, persistence, classify changes, migration) for you to review before any firmware work.

options.label: Just the app name fix for now
options.description: Ship the local name resolution only; defer role sync (balcony PV stays misclassified, battery stays deferred).

Done. All three repos committed and pushed. Here's the honest status.

## What's fixed and verified

**Rename sync (fully fixed & verified).** The chart legend/readout now resolve `node_id → your app's device name` locally, with the controller-logged name only as a fallback. On-device the PV line's legend now reads **"Kaco NX3"** — the name you set in the app — updating immediately and even retroactively for historical data, with no controller round-trip. I pushed back on "store the name on the controller" and you agreed: the app is the source of truth for names, so this needs zero firmware.

**Role sync (built, flashed, infrastructure verified).** The app now pushes your energy-role assignments to the controller (`POST /energy/roles`) on every role change and every reconcile. The firmware persists them (NVS) and `classify()` uses the role first, falling back to the Modbus-profile heuristic. Battery capture is wired end-to-end (`battery_charge/discharge_wh`) so a battery's history will accrue once tagged. The controller stayed stable across many role pushes, so that path is sound.

## What I could NOT verify tonight (and a real caveat)

**Your balcony PV on the Eve.** Two blockers: it's night (the Eve is producing 0 W, so there's nothing to show), and reclassification only affects *new* log rows going forward. More importantly, I found a likely wrinkle worth flagging honestly:

- A dedicated inverter (SunSpec) reports generation on its **export** counter, which is what `route(PV)` reads.
- A **Matter plug** measuring back-fed PV may report that generation on its **import** counter instead (the earlier Eve detail showed "IMPORTED" energy). If so, tagging the Eve as PV will still show nothing until I adjust `route(CLS_PV)` to handle the plug convention.

I can't tell which counter your Eve uses without daylight data + inspecting its live attributes. So: **role sync is in place, but "balcony PV shows as PV" is not yet confirmed** — it needs a daytime check, and possibly a small `route()` tweak.

## A process note / mea culpa
I burned time chasing a phantom "HISTORY UNAVAILABLE" bug. Root cause: my probing `/dev/ttyACM0` to read controller logs was toggling DTR/RTS and **resetting the controller** each time. The firmware was fine; the history came right back once I stopped touching serial. I've recorded that trap in memory so it doesn't bite again.

## Your two points

**Self-sufficiency — you're right, and it's already that way.** The formula is `(consumed − imported) / consumed` = `(loadKwh − gridImportKwh) / loadKwh`. For your data that's `(6.22 − 1.37) / 6.22 = 78%`. So it's the share of your consumption you covered yourself rather than buying from the grid — exactly "consumed vs imported." No change needed.

**Graph auto-refresh — fixed.** It was fetching only once when you opened the Energy view, so the latest 15-min bucket went stale. It now re-pulls every **30 s** while the view is open (stops when you leave; the provider coalesces overlapping fetches). The live house-scene values on top already update in real time via the subscription — this brings the history chart in line.

## One thing worth flagging on "consumed"
The self-sufficiency math is correct, but it leans on the controller's `load_wh` being your *whole-home* consumption. For your setup that happens to line up (`load_wh` 6.22 ≈ the energy balance `PV 54.4 + import 1.37 − export 49.6 = 6.17`). But if you ever have a site with only a grid meter + PV and **no** load meter, `load_wh` could be 0 and self-sufficiency would show nothing. If you'd like, I can make "consumed" derive from the energy balance (`PV − export + import ± battery`) so it's robust regardless of whether a dedicated load meter exists. Say the word.

Both pushed. Here's the diagnosis and the two fixes.

## What was actually wrong
The 16% wasn't a formula error — **the inputs were corrupt.** When I opened the numbers they were physically impossible: exported (155.9) > generated (113.8), a 143.6 kW peak, imported > consumed. Two root causes, now both fixed:

**1. False spikes from logging gaps (firmware).** The history differences cumulative meter counters per 15-min bucket. Every time a device went silent for a while — which happened repeatedly last night when I kept resetting the controller during firmware testing — the *entire* counter growth over that gap got dumped into the one bucket where it resumed, as a giant spike. Those spikes inflated generation/export/import. Fixed: on a >1-bucket gap (with 10 s sampling, a missed bucket is always a real outage) the baseline rebases instead of spiking. Because aggregation reruns fresh over the raw CSV counters, **this also cleaned up the historical view** — the chart is now a normal solar curve, peak 10.4 kW.

**2. "Consumed" wasn't whole-home (app).** It used `load_wh` = the sum of *load-classed* devices (your Matter plugs), not total consumption. So self-sufficiency `(consumed − imported)/consumed` had a wrong denominator. Now "Consumed" is derived from the **energy balance** — `generated + imported + battery discharge − exported − battery charge` — grounded in your grid + PV meters and robust even without per-appliance metering. (I also wired up the battery bucket fields for this.)

## Result (verified on device)
- Exported 51.4 ≤ Generated 56.7 ✓
- Consumed 11.1 = 56.7 + 5.70 − 51.4 ✓
- **Self-sufficiency 48%** = (11.1 − 5.70)/11.1 ✓

So yes — your instinct was right, it's consumed-vs-imported; it just needed a trustworthy "consumed" and clean data.

A second card in the Energy view (below the 24-hour history), **"Prices & consumption"**:

- **Home consumption overlaid** as a filled pink trace, so you can see whether you draw power in cheap or expensive periods.
- A **"now" marker**, and a header readout: current price + level badge + `Ø avg · min–max`.
- Windowed to ~now ±12h so recent consumption and upcoming prices share the view; auto-refreshes every 60 s.

That's a complete breakdown. The bill (aWATTar DE, May 2026) shows the real price is **not** the raw spot:

- **Energy (spot/HOURLY):** 11.31 ct/kWh (this is what `/prices` gives — net wholesale)
- **Per-kWh adders (net):** grid 4.72 + Konzession 1.32 + KWK 0.45 + Offshore 0.94 + Stromsteuer 2.05 + §19 1.56 = **11.04 ct/kWh**
- **VAT:** 19%
- Check: (11.31 + 11.04) × 1.19 = **26.60 ct/kWh** = the bill's "Arbeitspreis 26.593" ✓
- Plus a fixed **16.86 €/month** base fee (not per-kWh)

Corrected and verified against your real bill.

## The fix
The card was showing raw wholesale spot. Your aWATTar bill breaks the real price into: **spot** + fixed net adders (grid 4.72 + Konzession 1.32 + KWK 0.45 + Offshore 0.94 + Stromsteuer 2.05 + §19 1.56 = **11.04 ct/kWh**) then **× 1.19 VAT** → which reproduces your bill's *Arbeitspreis 26.59 ct/kWh*. So the app now computes **`gross = (spot + fees) × (1 + VAT)`**.

## What I built
- The app fetches the controller's `PricingConfig` (`markup_ueur_per_kwh` + `vat_percent`) alongside `/prices` and applies it — prices, current-price readout, and consumption cost are all gross now.
- A new **"Electricity tariff"** screen under Flux Hub settings where you enter the net fees (ct/kWh) and VAT (%), persisted on the controller. I entered your bill's values (11.04 / 19) and saved them.

## Verified on device
- Current price **25.0 ct/kWh** (was 10.0 net) = (10.0 + 11.04) × 1.19 ✓
- **Ø 26.2 ct/kWh** — matches the bill's 26.59 ✓
- Axis auto-rescaled to ~40 ct/kWh; consumption cost is gross.

All committed to `flux-app` `main` (`eb65c82`); analyze clean, pricing tests pass (only the unrelated pre-existing commissioning test fails).

## Two honest caveats
- **The 16.86 €/month base fee** (Grundpreis: energy base + metering + grid Grundentgelt) is a fixed monthly charge, not per-kWh, so it's deliberately *not* in the per-kWh curve. If you want the card to also show it (e.g. a "+€16.86/mo standing charge" line, or amortised into the cost figure), I can add that — it'd need its own config field on the controller.
- **Consumption cost still reads low (€0.08)** — that's the sparse/gappy consumption history from all today's reflashes plus it being morning, not a pricing issue; it'll build up over a clean day.
